https://www.nature.com/articles/s41746-0.name: PsychiatryBench
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41746-0.dataSource: Psychiatric casebooks, diagnostic manuals, and specialized clinical guides (DSM-5-TR Clinical Cases, Stahl's Essential Psychopharmacology, 100 Cases in Psychiatry, etc.) manually curated by licensed psychiatrists into 5,188 QA items
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41746-0.groundTruth: Expert-annotated answers based on reference text
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41746-0.evaluation: Automated grading for the closed-form tasks like MCQ/EMI/classification. LLM-as-judge framework (LLaMA 3.3 70B) that scores open-ended answers 0–100 for content similarity to the reference answer

https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.08584.name: CounselBench-Eval
https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.08584.dataSource: 100 real patient questions from CounselChat forum spanning 20 common mental health topics
https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.08584.groundTruth: Top-upvoted therapist replies serve as human baseline compared alongside LLMs
https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.08584.evaluation: 100 licensed mental health professionals rate each response across 6 clinical dimensions

https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.08584.name: CounselBench-Adv
https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.08584.dataSource: 120 adversarial questions generated by clinicians designed to elicit failure modes observed in CounselBench-Eval
https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.08584.groundTruth: Clear clinician-authored definitions and one in-context example per failure type
https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.08584.evaluation: 5 mental health professionals (separate from question authors) label each response for targeted failure

https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09189.name: Mental Health QA
https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09189.dataSource: USMLE-mental: 727 mental-health MCQs extracted from MedQA (USMLE Steps 1–2), keyword-filtered then author-reviewed. Crisis Response QA: 153 items authored from IACP (2018) and NAMI (2018) crisis manuals, GPT-4 created incorrect answers and medical students reviewed each question
https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09189.groundTruth: MCQ answer key based on MedQA + reference manuals

https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09189.name: Diagnosis Prediction - Online Text
https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09189.dataSource: SMHD: Reddit posts from users with one or more diagnosed mental-health conditions plus matched controls; the 16 most mental-health-relevant posts per user are retained; 500 users sampled (single- and multi-label).
https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09189.groundTruth: Diagnoses associated with each SMHD user
https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09189.evaluation: Automated classification accuracy againt diagnostic labels for each user
https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09189.population: Reddit users with self-reported mental health diagnoses and matched controls

https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09189.name: Diagosis Prediction - Dialogue
https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09189.dataSource: D4: ~130 multi-turn doctor-patient dialogues annotated with depression risk and suicide risk scores by clinicians
https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09189.groundTruth: Clinician-assigned depression-risk and suicide-risk scores (0-3) per dialogue
https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09189.evaluation: Automated accuracy against the clinician-assigned risk scores

https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09189.name: Psychological Counseling
https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09189.dataSource: PsyQA: Chinese online mental-health Q&A written by trained counselors/volunteers; 100 patient inquiries sampled, each paired with a support-strategy sequence.
https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09189.groundTruth: Professional mental health counselor responses serve as a human baseline alongside rubric-based empathy and safety ratings
https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09189.evaluation: GPT-4 as judge for response quality and EPITOME empathy (validated against human ratings); 8 human raters (qualification unstated) on a subset; fine-tuned BERT for dialogue safety.

https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.15297.name: Suicide Risk detection
https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.15297.dataSource: Simulated conversations produced by an AI user-agent role-playing personas with pre-defined suicide-risk levels, conversing with the chatbot under evaluation
https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.15297.groundTruth: ground truth is a clinician-developed suicide-risk-management rubric
https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.15297.evaluation: LLM judge-agent scores each simulated conversation against the rubric; scores aggregated per chatbot (rubric and agents undergoing clinician validation)

https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.15297.name: Evaluation of LLM Judge Agent Scoring
https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.15297.dataSource: Simulated conversations produced by an AI user-agent role-playing personas with pre-defined suicide-risk levels, conversing with the chatbot under evaluation
https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.15297.groundTruth: Ground truth are 3 clinican evaluation per prompt of LLM-agent responses to preditermined rubric
https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.15297.evaluation: Humans assessed differences in LLM evaluation vs. clinical evaluation of LLM generated responses.

https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PM.name: CAPE
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PM.dataSource: 4 most-popular psychotherapy custom GPTs on the OpenAI GPT Store, each probed with 2 fictional personas across the framework's 8 sections
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PM.groundTruth: No reference answers; ground truth is the CAPE rubric (8 sections, each scored 0-1)
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PM.evaluation: Human: 2 reviewers (incl. a psychiatrist) independently applied the CAPE framework; pairwise subscore differences tested (t tests, Wilcoxon)

https://doi.org/10.3390/diagnostics15222.name: StressSpeak
https://doi.org/10.3390/diagnostics15222.dataSource: Five public benchmark datasets: SAD (social-anxiety forum posts), Dreaddit (Reddit stress), DepSeverity (depression severity), SDCNL (suicide/depression counseling transcripts), and CSSRS-Suicide (Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale)
https://doi.org/10.3390/diagnostics15222.groundTruth: Gold: each dataset's annotated labels (stress presence/level, depression severity, suicide-risk level)
https://doi.org/10.3390/diagnostics15222.evaluation: Automated: accuracy, precision, recall, F1, FN/FP across 9 transformer models under zero-shot and few-shot settings; plus latency modeling and a 25-participant usability pilot
https://doi.org/10.3390/diagnostics15222.population: Social-media users, counseling clients, and suicide-severity-rated individuals (varied)

https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PM.name: CAPE-II
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PM.dataSource: 5 GenAI chatbots widely used by youth, probed by trained raters role-playing youth personas with mental-health challenges, across the CAPE-II framework's 9 sections
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PM.groundTruth: No reference answers; ground truth is the CAPE-II rubric (9 sections, binary high-quality ratings)
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PM.evaluation: Human: trained raters apply CAPE-II; proportion of high-quality ratings compared across chatbots (Bonferroni-corrected chi-square)

https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41875403.name: CapyEngine
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41875403.dataSource: 35 standardized case-scenario exam questions drawn from psychiatry and clinical-psychology board exams
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41875403.groundTruth: Gold: the board-exam correct diagnosis for each case
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41875403.evaluation: Automated diagnostic accuracy (correct answer within top-1/top-5/top-10) comparing CapyEngine, ChatGPT-4o, and 3 clinicians
